standard_prerequisites.name: A finite morphism is closed and has finite fibres, and the fibre of a finite morphism over a point of an affine base is finite

standard_prerequisites.name: Surjectivity of a map of quasi-coherent modules over an affine scheme after taking global sections, and the identification of global sections with the sum of the fibres at a finite set meeting every specialization class

standard_prerequisites.use: Produces a global section of the invertible module that does not vanish at any point of the fibre.

standard_prerequisites.name: Existence of a section of an invertible module on an affine scheme not vanishing at a prescribed finite set of points, cited from the properties chapter as the alternative to the direct argument given here
standard_prerequisites.use: The author offers it as the shortcut and then gives the direct argument that is counted here.

core_obligations: Reduce to an affine base: work with Y hence X affine, and record that the fibre of the finite morphism over the given point is finite (proof lines 3624-3626).

Produce a global section not vanishing on the fibre: choose a finite set of closed points meeting every specialization class of the fibre, use the surjection from the invertible module onto the sum of the fibres at those points, take global sections and use that this is exact in the affine case to get a section not vanishing at any point specializing to the chosen set (proof lines 3626-3646).

Push the nonvanishing locus down: the locus where the section does not vanish is an open neighbourhood of the fibre, and since the finite morphism is closed there is an open neighbourhood of the given point in the base whose preimage lies inside that locus, on which the section trivialises the invertible module (proof lines 3646-3652).
proof_roadmap: Work with an affine base and select a finite set of closed points meeting every specialization class of the finite fibre (proof lines 3624-3631).

Use surjectivity of evaluation at those points on global sections to find a section nonvanishing on the fibre, and push its nonvanishing locus down through the closed finite morphism (proof lines 3632-3652).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a finite morphism and an invertible module on its source, every point of the target has a neighbourhood over whose preimage the module is trivial (statement lines 3616-3622). The counted proof is a direct argument of moderate length: after reducing to an affine base it selects a finite set of closed points meeting every specialization class of the finite fibre, uses the surjectivity of evaluation at those points on global sections of the invertible module to obtain a section nonvanishing on the whole fibre, and then pushes the nonvanishing locus down through the closed finite morphism (proof lines 3624-3652). It is H2: the author explicitly notes that a cited properties chapter lemma would give the same section, but the direct argument is carried out in full inside the counted span.
